High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri H.S. Rathore - Govt. Advocate for the respondent /
Heard on I.A. No.19237/2024, which is first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for grant of suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant - Amir alias Aamir.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(3) of IPC r/w Section 3(2)(5) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred as "SC & ST Act")and sentenced to undergo L.I. with fine of Rs.5,000/-, Section 323 r/w Section 3(2)(5) of SC &
ST Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 6 months and Section 506 Part-2 r/w Section 3(2)(5A) of SC & ST Act and sentenced to under R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs.1,000/-, with default stipulation.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The prosecution's case is that on October 19, 2018, at about 11:00 PM, within the jurisdiction of the Industrial Area Police Station in Ratlam, the accused, Amir alias Aamir committed a heinous and repeated offense against a 16 years old minor prosecutrix.
It is alleged that the accused, who does not belong to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, knowingly targeted the victim due to her identity as a member of a Scheduled Caste.

The incident occurred in a washroom situated outside the victim's rented residence in Biriyakhedi, where the accused allegedly subjected her to repeated 2 CRA-3664-2024 penetrative sexual assault and aggravated penetrative sexual assault.

In addition to the sexual violence, the prosecution maintains that the accused wrongfully confined the victim,
voluntarily caused her physical hurt, and criminally intimidated her by issuing death threats to instill terror.
Accordingly, a case has been registered.

Learned counsel for the appellant argued that from the statement of the prosecutrix, it is clear that she was a consenting party however, since the family members reached at the spot, therefore, the report was lodged.
He further argued that the appellant has already undergone actual jail sentence of 7 years and 5 months, this appeal is of year 2024, final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
In such circumstances, this appellant is entitled for suspension of jail sentence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondent / State has opposed the present application and prays for its rejection.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and also taking into consideration the statement of the prosecutrix and the fact that appellant has already undergone actual jail sentence of more than 7 years and this appeal of year 2024 is not likely to be heard finally in near future, we are of the considered opinion that this appellant is entitled for grant of suspension of jail sentence.
Accordingly, I.A No.19237/2024 is allowed.

The jail sentence of appellant- Amir alias Aamir is suspended upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like 3 CRA-3664-2024 amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 13.05.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Registry.
Certified copy, as per rules.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA)

(ALOK AWAST  JUDGE JUDGE  Divyansh Ameer @ Aamir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94425144/
